description: This is a call for competition by Iarnród Éireann for the procurement of an experienced Design and Build Contractor to complete the design and deliver capacity enhancement and transformation works at Connolly Station. The project will create a new entrance from Preston Street and a passenger concourse within the historic Victorian undercroft, together with new lifts, escalators and staircases providing improved access to Platforms 5, 6 and 7. The works will also include additional emergency escape routes, public-realm improvements, retail, operational and back-of-house spaces, heritage refurbishment, structural alterations and the installation or modification of station and railway systems. The successful Contractor will be required to review and develop the reference design through detailed design to Approved for Construction status and subsequently construct, test and commission the works. The Contractor will also be responsible for providing complete as-built and handover information. The project will be delivered within a constrained, live operational railway environment. The Contractor will be required to manage passenger circulation, railway access, construction phasing, safety assurance, stakeholder engagement, heritage requirements and interfaces with other DART+ contracts. The appointed Contractor will undertake the role of Project Supervisor for the Construction Stage. The form of contract is currently anticipated to be the NEC4 Engineering and Construction Contract, Option C, target contract with activity schedule. title: KA-BAND SATELLITE TERMINAL PROTOTYPING FOR FUTURE RAILWAY MOBILE COMMUNICATION SYSTEM (FRMCS) (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 7C.093) - RE-ISSUE
description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to design, develop and validate in a lab environment a Ka-band satellite terminal prototype (i.e., modem and antenna) allowing to offer 5G NR FRMCS services via satellite while equipped on trains. Targeted Improvements: Ensure by 2030 the 100% coverage of railway lines by FRMCS and the consistency of passenger safety among the whole line. Description: The Future Railway Mobile Communication System (FRMCS), being a successor of the GSM-R system, is planned to be operational before GSM-R's predicted saturation in 2030. satcom is already established as a component of the future system and extensive work already took place to trade-off the best candidate satellite scenarios for the FRMCS servicing. Among the various options considered in terms of frequency bands, satellite orbit and air interface, the work concluded that one of the most promising and mature scenarios for immediate service is a 5G NR transparent GEO system in the Ka-band. Nevertheless, specific 5G NR terminals that mitigate the particularities of the railway environment for such satellite system are currently not available. This activity will therefore pave the way for such a terminal, by designing and developing a HW-based, Ka-band satellite terminal prototype for future usage on board of trains and 5G NR FRMCS communication connectivity via satellite. The HW-based terminal prototype will include both a 5G NR FRMCS modem and a satellite antenna integrated [FDP1] as necessary to form a complete solution. The activity will be supported by existing literature and on-going ESA activities, which highlight the best 5G NR configurations (e.g., numerologies, multiplex scheme), the best antenna solutions (e.g., parabolic vs. flat panel) and the best train installation options (e.g., single vs. dual antenna) for the mitigation of the channel impairments. These technical conclusions will be incorporated into the HW based modem and antenna solutions to form a state-of-the-art integrated terminal prototype. The integrated prototype shall use and/or upgrade COTS components (e.g., 5Gmodem parts, railway broadband antennas, RF front ends), and integrate them as necessary to adapt to the particularities of the satellite scenario. In addition, it shall be able to offer connectivity with existing transparent GEO satellites of today, without requiring modifications to the space segment and the feeder ground network component. The integrated solution however shall be able to achieve the demanding performance requirements of FRMCS despite the challenging railway-to- -satellite channel. The performance of the developed terminal prototype shall be validated in a laboratory environment with extensive testing under various realistic channel conditions.
